audit_findings.title: An unrecorded $84.7 million tax claim could sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: filed assessment over $84.7m; actual loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement not included in future OE requires an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2022, the Mexican federal tax authority issued a tax assessment on the Company’s subsidiary in Mexico for fiscal 2016 import taxes, value added taxes and custom processing fees of over $ 17.0 million, plus surcharges, fines and penalties of over $ 67.7 million for a total assessment of over $ 84.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved contingency, not a demonstrated liability. The company says loss is neither probable nor remote and cannot estimate a loss range. The stated $84.7m equals 56.8% of $149.0m anchor OE, 3.7% of $2,262m base equity value, or $4.58 per diluted share. That stated amount alone would not close the $152.81-per-share gap between base value and market price, but the filing provides no upper loss estimate, so materiality cannot be conclusively bounded.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest court status and a counsel-supported probability-weighted settlement range; deduct the expected payment from the bridge unless explicitly included in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Existing environmental-remediation cash obligations may be omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed liability $30.547m; filed net current-dollar anticipated costs $34.252m; unrecorded escrow $6.1m
audit_findings.mechanism: Reserve-funded remediation payments can bypass future expense and therefore require a bridge deduction to the extent not represented in projected OE, net of recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has accrued certain costs related to ongoing and potential future environmental investigation, monitoring and remediation activities at certain sites, as it has been determined that the costs are probable and can be reasonably estimated.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is recorded in the accounts but is not separately shown in the valuation bridge. That omission is not automatically a value error because OE retains accretion and revisions and may capture some cash runoff. Even deducting the entire latest $30.547m liability would reduce base equity value by only 1.35%, or $1.65 per share, before recognizing the $6.1m escrow asset. This cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile projected remediation payments to environmental expense, accretion and any working-capital adjustments in OE; deduct only the uncovered residual and add the restricted escrow if otherwise omitted.

audit_findings.title: Nuclear decommissioning obligations are not shown in the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: The eventual decommissioning principal is a senior cash claim and belongs in the equity bridge unless its cash outlay is explicitly included in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recognized as a liability the present value of the estimated future costs to decommission its nuclear laundry facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although the resulting value error depends on whether decommissioning cash flows were already forecast. A full $19.309m deduction is 0.85% of $2,262m base equity value, or $1.04 per diluted share. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether forecast OE includes decommissioning payments; otherwise deduct $19.309m, while avoiding duplication of retained accretion expense or related capital spending.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded SERP may be an omitted debt-like claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed projected benefit obligation $23.479m with no plan assets
audit_findings.mechanism: Past-service benefit payments reduce equity value unless the cash payments are captured in projected OE; annual pension expense alone does not necessarily settle the obligation.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company maintains an unfunded Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan (“SERP”) for certain eligible employees of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is filed and omitted from the stated bridge, but whether that omission overstates value depends on the treatment of benefit payments in OE. Deducting the full $23.479m would reduce base equity value by 1.04%, or $1.27 per diluted share, which cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map the filed benefit-payment schedule against pension expense and funding included in OE; deduct any settlement amount absent from projected cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Recurring contract-acquisition cash costs may be deferred out of the OE numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: computed FY2025 deferred-asset increase $7.744m; filed balance $104.679m and amortization $19.661m
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE recognizes only commission amortization, current cash commissions capitalized as contract assets are omitted from the OE numerator, overstating normalized OE and every discounted forecast year.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company defers commission expenses paid to its employee-partners when the commissions are deemed to be incremental for obtaining the route servicing customer contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting deferral is demonstrated, while omission from the OE calculation remains to be verified. The deferred balance rose from $96.935m to $104.679m in FY2025, a $7.744m increase equal to 5.2% of $149.0m anchor OE. It rose another $6.094m to $110.773m during the first 39 weeks of FY2026 while $15.895m was amortized. The recurring pattern is reasonably capable of materially lowering normalized OE because the valuation scales directly with the OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every historical OE worksheet for capitalized commissions or contract-asset changes; replace amortization-only treatment with cash commissions paid, or subtract the verified net capitalization, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A material control weakness affects several core OE inputs
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential errors in revenue, receivables, inventory or merchandise in service could affect reported earnings, reinvestment, working capital and the OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Management has identified a material weakness related to ineffective information technology (“IT”) controls over user access and change management related to the IT systems that support the revenue, accounts receivable, inventory, and merchandise in service processes.
audit_findings.explanation: The control weakness remained open at May 30, 2026, with some inventory and merchandise-control testing expected to continue into fiscal 2027. This is a present reliability issue, not merely a forward-looking risk, but neither management nor the auditor identified a financial-statement misstatement; the FY2025 statements received an unqualified opinion after additional procedures. The record therefore demonstrates deficient controls but not an OE error or its magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the fiscal 2026 remediation conclusion, auditor testing results, identified adjustments and later balance comparisons; rerun affected OE years if any revenue, receivable, inventory or merchandise corrections emerge.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: computed residual approximately $1.4m in FY2021 and $18.0m in FY2023; eligible portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE and could alter the anchor or growth evidence.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $104.6m (98.7% of filed D&A); FY2023 $103.2m (85.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is conservative treatment, not a demonstrated overvaluation. Using the supplied identified amounts and filed composites leaves approximately $1.4m in FY2021 and $18.0m in FY2023 unadded; the FY2023 residual is about 12.1% of the $149.0m anchor OE. However, the record does not establish that any residual is eligible, recurring or applicable to FY2025, so its valuation materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filed asset-class depreciation and amortization schedules, classify each residual component under the OE policy, and rerun the affected historical series and scenarios only for amounts proven eligible.
